name: Ronni Zehavi
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, HiBob (HR software, London/Tel Aviv/New York)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur who co-founded HiBob in Tel Aviv in 2015, maker of the 'Bob' cloud HR/HCM platform for mid-sized, distributed companies. HiBob has raised several $150M rounds (valued ~$2.7B in 2023) and has added payroll (Pento, 2024) and FP&A (Mosaic, 2025) via acquisitions. He remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Before HiBob he co-founded content-delivery startup Cotendo in January 2008 (backed by Sequoia and Benchmark), which Akamai bought in March 2012 for over $300M - he calls HiBob his third company.
deep_cut_fact: Cotendo was founded by three former Commtouch (later Cyren) colleagues - Zehavi, Udi Trugman and David Drai - with R&D in Netanya, Israel and HQ in Sunnyvale; it set out to challenge Akamai and ended up being acquired by it.
notes: No published press email found on hibob.com; press page and general Contact Us form are the official routes. Frequent podcast guest on HR/future-of-work topics (Josh Bersin, Digital HR Leaders, DealMakers).

name: Matthew Thompson
current_role: President & Chief Commercial Officer, Socure (identity verification), since Dec 2025
profile: Former Army Ranger and Harvard MBA who co-founded ID.me (begun 2010 as TroopSwap, a military deals site) with HBS classmate Blake Hall and served as its COO/president; left in 2015. Later ran IDEMIA's North America identity business and held an identity role at Capital One, then joined Socure, building its public-sector business before becoming CRO and, in Dec 2025, President & CCO.
interesting_fact: ID.me began as an HBS project: Hall and Thompson, both Army veterans, struggled to claim veteran discounts online. Thompson had gone to Goldman Sachs in Los Angeles after his MBA but came back when Hall opened shop near D.C. in early 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three patents spanning mobile biometric liveness detection and tiered and third-party authentication, and was Socure's first public-sector leader, launching its government business.
notes: No longer at ID.me (left 2015 per Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ID.me); best route is via Socure's PR agency (Highwire). Common name - confirm via ID.me/Socure context.

name: Roman Itskovich
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Risk Officer, At-Bay (cyber insurance, Mountain View/Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli-born co-founder of At-Bay (2016, with CEO Rotem Iram), a cyber insurer that pairs policies with active security monitoring ('insure-sec'). At-Bay has raised ~$295M from backers including Khosla, Lightspeed and M12 and reached unicorn status. As Chief Risk Officer he runs underwriting/risk and speaks publicly on cyber-market pricing discipline.
interesting_fact: At-Bay made Forbes' Fintech 50 list in 2023; Itskovich has publicly warned that 'irresponsible' competition in the cyber insurance market is unsustainable as threats rise.
deep_cut_fact: Before insurance he was VP of Financial Products at FX fintech Ebury, on Bain Capital's investment team, and a McKinsey consultant; he holds a BA in Economics and Accounting from Tel Aviv University and an HBS MBA.
notes: Has appeared on insurance podcasts (Behind the Growth, Making Risk Flow) - receptive to talking about cyber risk. Route via press@at-bay.com.

name: Mohit Garg
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, OLOID (passwordless workforce identity, Sunnyvale CA); co-founder of Mindtickle
profile: One of four co-founders (with Krishna Depura, Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali) of Pune-born Mindtickle, which pivoted from gamification to onboarding to sales enablement and became a unicorn in Aug 2021. In 2018 he co-founded OLOID, a passwordless/physical-identity platform for frontline workers, which has raised ~$23M Series A/A1 from Dell Technologies Capital, Honeywell, Okta Ventures and Yaletown.
interesting_fact: Mindtickle was the product of three pivots: it began in 2011 as a gamification platform, moved to employee onboarding, then to sales-rep productivity before reaching a $1B+ valuation.
deep_cut_fact: The Mindtickle idea began with online 'treasure hunts' the founders ran for fun - they later converted those treasure hunts into a way to engage and onboard new employees.
notes: Now focused on OLOID rather than Mindtickle (listed as Mindtickle co-founder/advisor). Appeared on Founder Thesis podcast ('Once Tickled, Twice OLOID'). No dedicated press email found; OLOID site has Contact Us form/newsroom.

name: Sean Henry
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Stord (commerce enablement / fulfillment, Atlanta)
profile: Atlanta native who co-founded Stord with Jacob Boudreau in 2015 as a Georgia Tech freshman, dropping out at 19. Stord provides warehousing, fulfillment and software that give independent brands Amazon-like shipping; a $250M Series F reportedly valued it around $3B. Thiel Fellow, Forbes 30 Under 30 (2019) and named by Forbes in 2021 the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company.
interesting_fact: Forbes recognized him in 2021 as the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company; he founded Stord at 18.
deep_cut_fact: The Stord idea crystallized days before his first Georgia Tech classes, while telling his family about his summer job at a manufacturer in Germany. He also dropped out before learning he'd won the Thiel Fellowship: 'I jumped two feet in and hoped they said yes later.'
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder (Entrepreneur bylines, Not Another CEO interview). Logistics/supply-chain angle fits the podcast.

name: Akhil Gupta
current_role: Co-founder, NoBroker Technologies (Bengaluru proptech) - widely described as its CTO; not independently confirmed here
profile: IIT alumnus who co-founded NoBroker in 2013 with Amit Kumar Agarwal and Saurabh Garg as a broker-free portal connecting flat owners and tenants. It expanded into resale, home services, the NoBrokerHood society-management app and the CallZen.AI conversational-intelligence tool, raised ~$361M (Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Google) and became a unicorn in Nov 2021.
interesting_fact: NoBroker runs a consumer-to-consumer real-estate model; by 2022 it handled 500,000+ transactions a year with over 7.5 million properties registered, and its NoBrokerHood app became part of India's ONDC network.
notes: Co-founder Amit Agarwal is the public face/CEO; Akhil Gupta is lower-profile. Web-search quota ran out, so no sourced deep-cut fact. Common name - check NoBroker context.

name: Anand Prakash
current_role: Co-founder & Head of Academics, Vedantu (Bengaluru edtech) - per Wikipedia; current status not independently confirmed
profile: IIT alumnus and co-founder (with Vamsi Krishna, Pulkit Jain and Saurabh Saxena) of Vedantu, launched in 2014, a live online tutoring platform for Indian school students (grades 4-12, plus JEE/NEET prep) that reached unicorn valuation in 2021. He has led academics/content at the company.
interesting_fact: The name Vedantu comes from the Sanskrit words 'Veda' (knowledge) and 'Tantu' (network).
deep_cut_fact: Before Vedantu, the same founding team built Lakshya, an IIT-JEE coaching institute, which was acquired by MT Educare (a Zee Learn affiliate) in 2012.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Vamsi Krishna is the company's main spokesperson. No published press email found (vcare is customer support). Common name in India - confirm via Vedantu context. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane.

name: Daniel Katz
current_role: Co-founder, A24 (independent film/TV studio, New York)
profile: Co-founded A24 in August 2012 with David Fenkel and John Hodges, with seed money from Guggenheim Partners. A24 grew from a distributor (Spring Breakers, Ex Machina, Room) into a producer behind Moonlight, Everything Everywhere All at Once, The Whale and The Brutalist, plus TV, music and a membership program. He remains a key executive and is famously press-shy.
interesting_fact: A24's 2023 Oscars sweep (Everything Everywhere All at Once won Best Picture among 7 Oscars, The Whale won two) came even as its founders shun the spotlight and almost never give interviews.
deep_cut_fact: The name 'A24' comes from Italy's Autostrada A24 (Rome-Teramo), which Katz was driving on when he decided to start the company.
notes: Extremely private - A24 founders rarely speak publicly; expect outreach through A24 publicity to be declined. Common name - this is the A24 co-founder.

name: Jason Ballard
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, ICON (3D-printed construction, Austin TX)
profile: Texas entrepreneur who founded sustainable home-improvement store TreeHouse (2011) before co-founding ICON, which 3D-prints homes and structures. ICON built Wolf Ranch near Georgetown, TX (billed as the world's largest 3D-printed community), printed US Army barracks, works with NASA on lunar/Martian construction, and launched the AI design tool Vitruvius. Named to TIME100 Next (2021) and TIME Trailblazers (2026).
interesting_fact: ICON partnered with NASA to print a simulated Martian habitat (Mars Dune Alpha) at Johnson Space Center and is developing technology for building on the Moon.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in hurricane-prone Bridge City/Orange, Texas (his family once spent Christmas in a FEMA trailer), he first entered discernment to become an Episcopal minister, then studied conservation biology at Texas A&M, earned a master's in space resources and apprenticed as a carpenter.
notes: Charismatic public speaker (SXSW 2022 featured talk 'It's Time To Build'). Do not confuse with Virginia politician Jason Ballard. No published press email found; use ICON contact form/newsroom.

name: Maulik Majmudar
current_role: Chief Medical Officer, Biofourmis (AI-driven in-home care / remote monitoring, Boston)
profile: Physician executive listed on Biofourmis' executive team as Chief Medical Officer (MD). Biofourmis, founded in 2015 in Singapore and now Boston-based, builds AI-driven remote patient monitoring and hospital-at-home programs; it sold its life-science business to ActiGraph and merged with CopilotIQ. Hurun lists him as a founder, but Biofourmis' site presents him as CMO rather than a co-founder.
interesting_fact: Biofourmis merged with CopilotIQ to create what they called the first end-to-end platform for AI-driven in-home care.
notes: Founder status questionable: Biofourmis is generally credited to Kuldeep Singh Rajput; Majmudar appears as CMO (https://biofourmis.com/about). Widely reported (not verified here) that he previously was a cardiologist at Massachusetts General Hospital and a principal medical officer at Amazon - confirm before using. No press email found.

name: Michael Frizell
current_role: Co-founder of Pet Circle (Sydney online pet retailer), long-time CEO (current title not re-verified)
profile: Mike Frizell co-founded Australian online pet-supplies retailer Pet Circle with James Edwards in mid-2011. It grew 300%+ between 2013 and 2015, raised A$125M Series C in Dec 2021 at a valuation above $1B, added pet insurance in 2023 and secured a further $75M that year to fund expansion.
interesting_fact: Pet Circle was named on Deloitte's list of fastest-growing technology companies in Nov 2014, and Frizell was a finalist in EY's Entrepreneur of the Year Awards in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: The company started life in 2011 under a different name - 'Paws for Life' - and only rebranded to Pet Circle in early 2014.
notes: Pet Circle site rate-limited (429) during research so no press email captured; check petcircle.com.au footer/media page. Goes by 'Mike Frizell'.
